overview: White develops the bishop to b5 on move two, inviting a Ruy Lopez-style game with the e6 pawn already played. Black can reply 2...c6 3.Ba4 d5 or 2...Nf6 and reach a sound French-like or Sicilian-like position with a free game, since the bishop does little here. I am unsure of the main reply but the line is a rare sideline.

white_ideas.idea: Continue with Nf3, d4 or c3 and keep the bishop active on the a4-e8 diagonal.
Hope Black moves the pawns so that Bxc6 or a quick d4 gives an edge.

black_ideas.idea: Challenge the centre with ...c6 and ...d5, gaining time against the bishop.
Develop with ...Nf6 and ...d5 and reach a normal French structure.

typical_structures.structure: French pawns on e6 and d5 against e4, with White's bishop misplaced on a4 or b5.

character.notes: Quiet, with no forcing tactics; Black has an easy game.

soundness.notes: Not refuted but loses time; I judge it sound but passive.

structure.notes: French-type e4 against ...d5; the centre opens or locks depending on later moves.

approach.notes: A rare early bishop sortie that strong players hardly play.

level.notes: Few theory demands, but not a recommended first repertoire.
